initiative.title: Terminal Status Start Guard
initiative.summary: Prevent taskset dispatch from selecting or restarting closed and released work records.

taskset.summary: Align taskset terminal-status selection and start transitions with the established closed/released status vocabulary.

tasks.title: Block taskset restart of closed and released records
tasks.goal: Make closed/released tasks and their registered Korean aliases terminal in taskset selection and start persistence.
tasks.scope: Change only taskset_dispatcher terminal-status membership and start-target behavior, its generated-host mirror, focused regressions, and the host lock. Do not redesign the shared status schema or change unrelated status consumers.
acceptance: Taskset planning does not select closed, released, 종결, 종료, 릴리스됨, or 배포됨 task records as actionable work.
The start-target helper returns no transition for every closed/released canonical value and registered alias.
Existing planned/active/localized start behavior and completed/done terminal behavior remain unchanged.
Root/template parity and the generated-host lock remain current.

units.title: Treat closed and released task statuses as terminal
units.context: TASK-AR-604 skeptic verification found a pre-existing counterexample: _target_status_for_work_start maps closed/released and the aliases 종결/종료/릴리스됨/배포됨 back to in_progress. The same dispatcher-local DONE_STATUSES set omits these terminal values, so selection can also treat them as actionable.
units.scope: Add failure-first selection and transition coverage, then make only the dispatcher-local terminal checks recognize closed/released and their aliases. Preserve the shared status schema and other consumers.
steps: Reproduce terminal records being selected or mapped to an in-progress start target.
Align dispatcher-local terminal membership and start-target behavior with normalized closed/released values.
Mirror the runtime implementation and regenerate the host lock.
Run focused tests, parity, lock, taskset gates, W4a, independent W4b, and skeptic review.
acceptance: All six canonical/alias terminal cases are no-select and no-transition paths.
No global status vocabulary or unrelated consumer changes are included.
units.handoff: Report failure-first evidence, terminal selection/start matrix, focused tests, template parity, host lock, and independent review.
units.stop_condition: Stop if the fix requires changing the shared schema or any status consumer outside taskset_dispatcher.
